## Statement · **draft**
Let $G$ be a finite group with $|G| = p^{a} m$, where $p$ is a prime and $p \nmid m$. A subgroup of $G$ of order $p^{a}$, call it $P$, is called a **Sylow $p$-subgroup**.

Equivalently, $P$ is, in $G$, a **maximal $p$-subgroup** (under inclusion). The set of all Sylow $p$-subgroups is denoted $\operatorname{Syl}_p(G)$; if $P \in \operatorname{Syl}_p(G)$, then $[G : P] = m$.
